messages:
liam-sales: Heads up — vendor NebulaData (Ireland) submitted an invoice but flagged that their subcontractor in Spain requires withholding. They're asking Redwood to gross-up.
maria-finance: We need clarity: non-US vendor + non-US subcontractor. Do they want Redwood to gross-up for Spanish withholding or will vendor handle netting?
liam-sales: Vendor's AP note: 'Please pay gross amount and reimburse withholding to subcontractor' attached invoice.
maria-finance: Upload the invoice snippet?
liam-sales: Attached in portal. Snippet:
```
Invoice #ND-2026-132
Vendor: NebulaData Limited (IE) - VAT IE6388047V
Subcontractor: DataLabs SL (ES)
Amount (net): EUR 15,000
Note: Spanish withholding 19% applies to non-resident provision; vendor requests payer gross-up.
```
anya-tax: Spanish withholding on services generally depends on residency. If subcontractor is Spanish tax resident with a tax id (NIF), withholding may not apply. We need subcontractor's Spanish tax certificate or a declaration. Also for cross-border VAT, reverse-charge may apply — need VAT invoice fields.
maria-finance: So ask vendor for: 1) subcontractor's Spanish tax residency docs (NIF + certificate), 2) copy of subcontractor contract showing payment terms, 3) breakdown showing gross-up calculation and legal basis.
josh-payments: Also need correct bank beneficiary details — current USD bank in invoice doesn't match portal. payment holds until docs are verified.
vendor-bot: Automated request sent to ap@nebuladata.ie for: subcontractor NIF + certificate, gross-up attestation, signed VAT invoice. Delivery: delivered.
liam-sales: Vendor replied: 'Subcontractor is Spanish but we are reluctant to share its TRC. We'll provide a signed attestation saying we request gross-up and will accept a reimbursement schedule.'
anya-tax: That's not sufficient. We need evidence of withholding and tax authority citation or TRC. Otherwise Redwood can't accept an open gross-up liability. If they insist, request a signed indemnity and calculation certified by vendor's tax advisor.
maria-finance: We won't alter our tax withholding policy without proper docs. If subcontractor can't provide TRC, vendor must absorb withholding or provide an indemnity with VAT/withholding calculation.
josh-payments: Flagging for manager approval to allow partial release if they provide interim docs. @maria-finance can you confirm thresholds?
maria-finance: Manager pre-approval requires: signed attestation, certified gross-up worksheet, and PO match. Then we can authorize 75% release via expedited ACH; remainder upon final docs.
liam-sales: I'll ask vendor to either re-issue invoice as net (vendor absorbs withholding) or upload TRC + certified calc. They asked if Redwood can issue an intermediary payment to subcontractor — we don't do third-party pay.
anya-tax: Also request a W-8/W-9 equivalent? For EU vendors, vendor should supply local tax residency docs; US forms not applicable.
vendor-bot: Reminder: please upload documents to vendor portal to avoid manual email attachments.
liam-sales: Vendor acknowledged and will upload within 48 hours.
maria-finance: Great. Closing note: Any gross-up acceptance must include line-by-line math (gross, withholding %, amount withheld, net to subcontractor) and reference to Spanish legal article/regulation. No generic statements.
josh-payments: Noted. I'll keep the payment on hold and update the queue once files appear.
liam-sales: Will follow up and report back here.
